patches.old: Choice D reverses the two theorists' contributions, which is the most tempting distractor since students sometimes confuse the number of factors associated with each theorist.
patches.new: Choice D is the most tempting distractor, but note what it actually does: the three broad superfactors belong to Eysenck, not Cattell, and the sixteen factors belong to Cattell, not Allport — so it misassigns both numbers rather than simply swapping this question's two theorists.

sources.title: OpenStax, Psychology §11.7 — trait theorists, covering Allport's categories, Cattell's 16 factors, the Eysencks' dimensions and the five factor model

visual.title: The four models and Eysenck's arousal claim
visual.alt: Four cards tracing the trait tradition from Allport's lexical sorting through Cattell's sixteen source traits and Eysenck's three supertraits to the five factor model; a list of the OCEAN dimensions with what each one predicts; and a panel setting out Eysenck's two biological claims, that introverts begin from higher cortical arousal and therefore prefer quiet while extraverts seek input, and that neuroticism reflects limbic reactivity.
visual.caption: Introverts start high on the arousal dial, which is why the quiet room suits them. Reversing that is the single commonest error on this topic.
